title: Infinitesimal line bundles on a split thickening and their cocycles
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], put $A=k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ [def-sc-dual-numbers], and let $X_A=X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}A$ with projection $p:X_A\to X$ and closed inclusion $j:X\hookrightarrow X_A$ [def-pc-base-change]. Write $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ for the group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules under tensor product [def-sc-invertible-module]. There is a canonical isomorphism of abelian groups
$$\beta_X:H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)\xrightarrow{\sim}\ker\bigl(j^*:\operatorname{Pic}(X_A)\to\operatorname{Pic}(X)\bigr),$$
with module cohomology as in [pqf-def-cohomology]. For an open covering $\{U_i\}$ and an additive Cech cocycle $c_{ij}\in\mathcal O_X(U_i\cap U_j)$, $\beta_X$ sends its image in $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ to the line bundle glued by transition units $1+\epsilon c_{ij}$. In particular, if $L$ is invertible on $X$ and $L_A$ is invertible on $X_A$ reducing to $L$, and local frames have transition functions $t_{ij}$ for $L$ and $t_{ij}(1+\epsilon c_{ij})$ for $L_A$, then $[L_A\otimes p^*L^{-1}]=\beta_X([c_{ij}])$. This description is natural for pullback and for $\epsilon\mapsto\lambda\epsilon$; tensor product corresponds to addition of cohomology classes. When $k$ is separably closed and $X$ is a smooth projective geometrically integral curve with a $k$-point and represented Picard functor [def-sc-picard-functor], the canonical Picard tangent identification [lem-sc-pic-tangent-space] sends the tangent vector represented by $\beta_X(v)$ to $v$ (using the same transition-function convention).

source.place: Tag 0C6R, lemma-picard-group-first-order-thickening and proof, specialized to the split thickening O_X[epsilon]; transition cocycles via cohomology.tex lemma-h1-invertible. Compatibility with the represented Picard tangent: literature/milne-abelian-varieties_AV.pdf, Chapter III Proposition 2.1, pp.90–91, map a -> 1+a epsilon.

proof.text: Identify the underlying spaces of $X_A$ and $X$ by $j$. On an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ the thickening is $\operatorname{Spec}R[\epsilon]$; every prime contains $\epsilon$, and primes and basic opens correspond under reduction. Its structure sheaf on this space is $\mathcal O_X\oplus\epsilon\mathcal O_X$: on a basic open this follows from $R[\epsilon]_f=R_f[\epsilon]$, and the identifications agree on restrictions and hence glue. Thus this description holds on arbitrary opens, without a separatedness or finiteness assumption.

source.place: Tag 0C6R, split first-order thickening; affine description of the dual-number base change

proof.text: Write $F=\mathcal O_{X,ab}$, $G=\mathcal O_X^\times$ and $E=\mathcal O_{X_A}^\times$ on the common space. There is a split exact sequence of abelian sheaves $0\to F\xrightarrow{e}E\xrightarrow{r}G\to0$, where $e(a)=1+\epsilon a$, $r(u+\epsilon v)=u$, and the section is $s(u)=u$. Indeed $u+\epsilon v$ is a unit exactly when $u$ is, with inverse $u^{-1}-\epsilon u^{-2}v$. The retraction $d:E\to F$ is $d(u+\epsilon v)=u^{-1}v$; multiplication gives $d(zz')=d(z)+d(z')$. In particular $de=1$, $re=0$, $rs=1$, and $e(d(z))s(r(z))=z$. These formulas commute with every restriction.

source.place: Tag 0C6R, lemma-picard-group-first-order-thickening, proof: the map f to 1+f; explicit split case

proof.text: Use the long exact cohomology sequence supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] for global sections of abelian sheaves; the required category, enough injectives and derived-cohomology convention are those of [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Since $s$ splits $r$ on global sections, the boundary $H^0(G)\to H^1(F)$ is zero. Exactness therefore makes $H^1(e)$ an isomorphism onto $\ker H^1(r)$. Equivalently its inverse there is $H^1(d)$: the split identities in step 2 remain identities after the additive functor $H^1$, giving both inverse equations.

Apply [thm-sc-hilbert-90] to both schemes, using only its Zariski assertion $\operatorname{Pic}(Y)\simeq H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y^\times)$. By [lem-sc-picard-h1-restriction-compatibility] restriction along the closed immersion $j$ is the map induced by $r$, and the closed-pushforward cohomology identification in that statement is simply the common-space identification here. By [lem-sc-module-abelian-zariski-cohomology] the group $H^1(F)$ is the underlying additive group of the module cohomology $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ in the item. Compose these identifications with $H^1(e)$ of step 3 to define $\beta_X$. All arrows are the specified canonical maps, so this defines the claimed canonical group isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0C6R proof; cohomology.tex Tag 09NU lemma-h1-invertible; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03FD lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree

proof.text: The Zariski assertion and transition-section normalization of [lem-sc-torsor-h1] identify the image of the additive cocycle $(c_{ij})$ with the $F$-torsor having local sections $a_i$ satisfying $a_j=c_{ij}+a_i$. The coefficient-map assertion of [lem-sc-torsor-h1-functoriality], applied to $e:F\to E$, sends this to the $E$-torsor whose transition sections are $1+\epsilon c_{ij}$. Under [thm-sc-hilbert-90] this is the frame torsor of precisely the invertible module glued with those units. We fix the convention $m_j=(1+\epsilon c_{ij})m_i$; then the additive equation $c_{ik}=c_{ij}+c_{jk}$ is exactly the gluing equation, since $\epsilon^2=0$. This proves the cocycle formula on any open cover, using the comparison image rather than asserting that this cover computes all of $H^1$.

For the displayed deformation of $L$, tensor its chosen frame with the dual of the pulled-back frame of $L$. On an overlap its transition unit becomes $t_{ij}(1+\epsilon c_{ij})t_{ij}^{-1}=1+\epsilon c_{ij}$. The preceding step gives $[L_A\otimes p^*L^{-1}]=\beta_X([c_{ij}])$. Similarly tensoring two such frame systems multiplies their units and gives $1+\epsilon(c_{ij}+c'_{ij})$. Changing frames by $1+\epsilon h_i$ changes the coefficients to $c_{ij}+h_j-h_i$ (using the same frame convention), so the answer depends only on the cohomology class.

source.place: Tag 0B8R lemma-cech-h1, transition-section calculation; Tag 09NU lemma-h1-invertible

proof.text: To verify pullback explicitly, let $f:Y\to X$ be a $k$-morphism. Every class of $H^1(F)$ admits a cocycle on some open cover $U$: by [lem-sc-torsor-h1] it is represented by a torsor, and its local sections give such a cover. Put $V_i=f^{-1}U_i$ and take normalized comparison systems $c$ for $U$ and $c'$ for $V$ by [lem-pc-cech-comparison-system-existence]. Such a system is not unique, so first check that in degree one it computes the class of step 5. Let $T$ be the $F$-torsor glued from a cocycle $(a_{ij})$ on $U$, with sections $t_i$ over $U_i$ and $t_j=a_{ij}\cdot t_i$, and let $0\to F\to E_T\to\mathbf Z\to0$ be the sequence of [lem-sc-torsor-h1] whose connecting map sends $1$ to the class of $T$. It is surjective on sections over every tuple intersection $U_y$, since $n[t_{y(0)}]$ lifts a locally constant $n$. By the degree-zero normalization and the connecting-map law of [def-pc-cech-comparison-system], $c^1(\check\delta(1))=\delta(c^0(1))=\delta(1)=[T]$, and $\check\delta(1)$ is the cocycle $[t_j]-[t_i]=a_{ij}$. Hence $c^1([a])$ is the class used in step 5, for every cocycle and every system; the same holds on $Y$ for $c'$. By [lem-pc-cech-comparison-inverse-image-unit] the inverse-image part of cohomology pullback sends the cocycle $(c_{ij})$ to its inverse-image cocycle; here every $V$-tuple intersection equals the inverse image of the corresponding $U$-tuple intersection, so its covering hypothesis holds. Naturality of $c'$ in abelian sheaves then applies to $f^{-1}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Y$. Thus the resulting cocycle is $(f^\sharp c_{ij})$. These are exactly the coefficients of the pulled-back transition units $f_A^\sharp(1+\epsilon c_{ij})=1+\epsilon f^\sharp c_{ij}$. Step 5 on $Y$ proves $f_A^*\beta_X(v)=\beta_Y(f^*v)$. The module-to-abelian comparison is the canonical one from step 4; thus the pullback here is the usual cohomology pullback, not a newly chosen map.

source.place: Tag 0B8R lemma-cech-h1; canonical comparison and its inverse-image/coefficient naturality (Tag 01EQ lemma-cech-cohomology)

proof.text: Let $\sigma_\lambda$ be the endomorphism of $X_A$ induced by $\epsilon\mapsto\lambda\epsilon$. It sends the transition units $1+\epsilon c_{ij}$ to $1+\epsilon\lambda c_{ij}$, so by step 5 $\sigma_\lambda^*\beta_X([c])$ is $\beta_X$ of the class of $(\lambda c_{ij})$. Take a normalized comparison system on the cover by [lem-pc-cech-comparison-system-existence]; by step 7 it computes these classes, and its naturality in abelian sheaves [def-pc-cech-comparison-system], applied to multiplication by $\lambda$ on $F$, shows that the class of $(\lambda c_{ij})$ is $H^1(\lambda)$ of the class of $(c_{ij})$. Multiplication by $\lambda$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-module endomorphism, so by the naturality in [lem-sc-module-abelian-zariski-cohomology] $H^1(\lambda)$ is the module-cohomology map $H^1(X,\lambda)$, which is multiplication by $\lambda$ on the $k$-vector space $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Every class has the local representative used in step 7. Hence this pullback acts on $\beta_X(v)$ as $\beta_X(\lambda v)$. This includes $\lambda=0$, when the transition units are all $1$; it requires no division by $\lambda$.

source.place: Tag 0B8R lemma-cech-h1, coefficient naturality of the Cech comparison; Milne III Proposition 2.1, p.91

proof.text: Now impose the curve and representability hypotheses of the final clause. By [sk-prop-picard-pic-split], its smooth proper geometrically connected curve assertion applies (geometric integrality implies geometric connectedness), and the chosen rational point splits off the base Picard group, naturally on test schemes. For $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ these base Picard groups vanish: each space is one point, so an invertible module, being locally free of rank one, is free on the whole space. Consequently the kernel of the represented Picard functor on $A\to k$ is the actual kernel of $j^*$ used above. By the functor-of-points definition [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], this is the tangent space at the identity. Milne III Proposition 2.1 defines its canonical comparison with $H^1$ by the map induced by $a\mapsto\exp(\epsilon a)=1+\epsilon a$. This is exactly $e$ of step 2; therefore the inverse comparison sends $\beta_X(v)$ to $v$. Here the exponential formula specifies which canonical identification in [lem-sc-pic-tangent-space] is meant; we do not infer equality of specified maps from the mere existence of a linear isomorphism. Tensor and scalar compatibility from steps 6 and 8 give its stated linear convention.
